answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can bind each identity to a stake locked in a shared vault, where required collateral scales with how much a newcomer multiplies itself. Every agent grows trust the way a vine climbs a trellis: one supported segment at a time, through epochs of peer-graded, difficulty-stamped work rather than a single spoofed credential. An attacker spinning up hundreds of shells must fund hundreds of deposits yet only accrues trust at the network's natural pace, so fabrication costs more than it can siphon, and forfeiting the vault stake keeps the attack unprofitable.
